sections.h2: Selling a house in York, PA
sections.html:
York is a compact city in York County with about 45,342 residents and 17,893 households. Owners occupy 43.7 percent of homes, the midpoint home value is $119,700 and rent at the midpoint is $1,014 a month. The city's Bureau of Permits and Inspections decides several things a seller needs before closing, including tenant licenses and possibly a certificate of compliance.

The paperwork runs through an online permit system, and the office sees people by appointment only. Call before you plan a trip downtown.

sections.h2: City documents for a sale or rental
sections.html:
York City Bureau of Permits and Inspections documents
DocumentWhen it applies
Tenant occupied licenseTenant-occupied residential and institutional buildings, which are inspected before licensing
Certificate of ComplianceA structure changing ownership or tenancy without a change in use classification
Certificate of OccupancyNew construction, major renovations, reoccupying condemned structures, changes in occupancy
Electrical turn on permitNeeded before the utility restores service, with a DR number from Met-Ed

Call the Bureau at 717-849-2256 to confirm what a house sale requires. The office is at 101 S. George St., and appointments are made by phone. Permit applications must be filed before work begins, and permits now follow the 2021 Uniform Construction Code.

Before any inspection, collect the deed, any prior certificates, receipts for permitted work and the name of every tenant.

sections.h2: Selling a rental with a tenant occupied license
sections.html:
Rental owners in York carry a license that depends on an inspection. No checklist exists, so inspectors apply the City of York Property Maintenance Code, which is posted on the city website. Landlords prepare by reading the code itself.

  • Reinspections and the Consolidated Board of Appeals go through the tenant occupied administrative desk.
  • Typical complaints in the city include weeds over 10 inches, uncollected trash, pest problems, leaks, sewer backups and mold.
  • Neighborhood Improvement Ordinance tickets can be appealed, but the appeal form has to be mailed or hand-delivered, not emailed.
  • Property owners are responsible for the sidewalk and trees in front of the house.

A buyer who purchases rentals as-is will usually want the current license and any open citations in hand before settlement. Clear those, or disclose them in writing, before the contract.

sections.h2: Deed recording and transfer tax in York County
sections.html:
The York County Recorder of Deeds charges a realty transfer tax of 2 percent in total, 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to local governments. Documents go first to the county Assessment Office, which certifies the parcel number, and then to the Recorder for recording and fees. The sales contract decides whether buyer or seller pays, though both are liable. Ask the Recorder for the share that applies to a York City address.

  • You can record in person, by mail, or through Simplifile or Ingeo, with a stamped return envelope and payment for the fees.
  • One check may cover everything, or you can write three. Either is accepted.
  • A Statement of Value is required when you claim an exemption or pay a different amount than the deed states. It adds $2 to the recording fee.
  • A deed from a father to a son and similar family transfers are tax exempt if the deed states the relationship.
  • Recorded documents come back after about four to eight weeks, depending on workload.

Hurricane Agnes set the state's 24-hour precipitation record of 13.5 inches at the York weather station on June 22, 1972, so buyers do ask about basements. Plan to show a dry basement and sound gutters, and keep records of any sump pump work or waterproofing.

An as-is purchaser prices roof and foundation questions differently from a buyer who needs a loan, so say plainly what you know. Gather permit records for past work too. Electrical, plumbing, mechanical and demolition work in York City goes through the Bureau's online system, and sheds, decks and interior remodels need permits as well.

sections.h2: What buyers and investors look for
sections.html:
York has colleges and a large hospital system nearby, which keeps renters in the market, and the mean commute for York workers is 23.1 minutes, so sellers can market access to both Harrisburg and Baltimore. Investors pay close attention to licensing status and open citations, while owner-occupants focus on condition. Match your preparation to the buyer you expect.

If you plan a quick as-is sale, ask each buyer who handles the city paperwork, who pays recording costs and whether the offer depends on any inspection.

sections.h2: From contract to closing in York
sections.html:
Begin by calling the Bureau to learn what documents your property needs. Next, have the county Assessment Office certify the parcel number on the deed. Your title company or attorney then prepares the deed, and a Statement of Value if one is required. At settlement the deed is signed, fees and tax are paid, and the Recorder files it. Allow four to eight weeks for the recorded deed to come back, and enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

A cash buyer has no loan or appraisal, so the schedule depends on title work and city paperwork. Collect the deed, payoff figures and any tenant information while you wait for the appointment at the Bureau.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell my York house?
faqs.a: Possibly. A Certificate of Compliance applies to a structure changing ownership or tenancy without a change in use. Call 717-849-2256 to confirm what your address needs.

faqs.q: How much does York County charge in transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent in total, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to local governments. The sales contract decides whether buyer or seller pays.

faqs.q: Can I transfer a York house to a family member tax free?
faqs.a: Yes, when the deed states the family relationship, such as a transfer from a father to a son. Check with an attorney, and file a Statement of Value if you claim any other exemption.

faqs.q: How do I get a permit or license from York City?
faqs.a: Most applications are filed online through the city's OpenGov system. The Bureau of Permits and Inspections, at 101 S. George St., also takes appointments by phone at 717-849-2256.

faqs.q: How long until York County returns my recorded deed?
faqs.a: It takes about four to eight weeks after recording, because each document is scanned, proofed, indexed and verified. Include a stamped, self-addressed envelope.
